calls.body: At home, the Lightning keep sending Gourde’s line (Viel, Gourde and Geekie) out against opponents’ fourth lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Jon Cooper keeps choosing line for line. Tonight the Capitals’ fourth line is Ovechkin, Protas and Sourdif.

surprises.head: Washington couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: Washington usually gets some of the league’s most dangerous shots. Not tonight: a 4.7% chance of scoring on the average shot at 5-on-5, against their usual 7.0% and a league average of 6.4%. A team strays this far about once every 35 games.

story.head: Carlson has three assists as the Lightning take down the Capitals
paras: The first period was a wild one. Sam O'Reilly, in his fourth NHL game, scored his first NHL goal, set up by Jeffrey Viel, early in the period to open the scoring for the Lightning. Charle-Édouard D'Astous and Jake Guentzel scored two and a half minutes apart midway through the period to make it 3-0. Alex Tuch got the Capitals on the board just over three minutes later. The Bolts’ Zemgus Girgensons left late in the first period and didn’t return. Two days later, he was placed on injured reserve with an upper-body injury. Guentzel scored his second of the night midway through the second to make it 4-1 for the Lightning. Ryan Leonard cut Tampa Bay’s lead to 4-2 early in the third, and Anthony Cirelli added an empty-net goal with less than three minutes left to make it 5-2. John Carlson finished with three assists.
The Lightning had a bit more of the good stuff. Andrei Vasilevskiy made 25 saves for the Lightning, and Logan Thompson stopped 20 of 24 at the other end.

Only two penalties were called all night, something the league sees about once every 20 games. The Lightning improved to 14-5-2, still first in the Atlantic, while the Capitals fell to 10-9-0, fifth in the Metropolitan.

items.text: The Capitals are on a three-game losing streak.

The Lightning’s Nikita Kucherov played his 900th NHL game and had two assists.
The Lightning have beaten the Capitals four straight times, going back to last season.
